clue.text: Underwear malfunction

definitions.meaning: a woman's undergarment worn beneath a dress
a small error or failure, a lapse such as one of the tongue

explanation.surface: A wardrobe malfunction involving lingerie.
explanation.definitionFit: Slip names both a petticoat-like garment and a minor mistake or lapse.

clue.text: Team having shots at goal? Supporters will appear

parts.note: a side is a sports team
in football, shots at goal are kicks

explanation.surface: A football team taking shots draws its fans out to watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidekicks are loyal assistants or companions, those who back up a hero.

clue.text: Ask for endless row, endless, regarding some fertility treatments?

indicators.note: without its end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to invite someone is to ask them

indicators.note: again the end is cut, so the last letter goes

parts.note: taken as written, a line of things

explanation.surface: Asking for an unending argument about how IVF works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' twice cuts the last letter: INVIT and RO.
explanation.definitionFit: In vitro, Latin 'in glass', describes fertilisation done in a laboratory dish rather than in the body.

clue.text: Qualification Oxford, say, mostly backed, following protocols?

parts.note: a diploma is an academic qualification

indicators.note: backed means the shortened word runs in reverse
most of the word is kept, so its final letter goes

parts.note: Oxford is an example of a city

explanation.surface: An Oxford qualification sought by someone going by the book.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford is a city given by example ('say'); 'mostly' shortens it and 'backed' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Protocol is diplomatic etiquette, so acting according to it is behaving in a diplomatic way.

clue.text: My status is no longer single — but it's not good

definitions.text: My status is no longer single
definitions.meaning: I am now part of a couple
damaged or weakened, so in poor condition

explanation.surface: Someone announcing they are in a relationship, with a gloomy twist.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is read as two words, I'M PAIRED; the second as the single word IMPAIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impaired has been damaged or diminished, so it is in a bad state.

clue.text: Sucker expecting shelter to be offered by church

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A gullible person hoping a church will give them a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A leech is a bloodsucking worm, literally an animal that sucks.

clue.text: Suburbia: a term on departing London, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals these letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs, and L the usual one for London

explanation.surface: A commuter's season ticket out of the capital leads into the suburbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' shuffles A TERM ON together with D and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Metroland was the suburban belt north-west of London served by the Metropolitan Railway, so it stands for suburbia.

clue.text: Computer pioneer penning note forcing a change of direction

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as animals are shut in a pen

parts.note: Alan Turing was a founding figure of computer science
N, short for note

explanation.surface: A computing pioneer writing a memo that redirects things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' encloses N inside TURING.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning is the act of changing course, rotating to a new heading.

clue.text: Aeroplane, perhaps, caught offloading contents to accommodate airmen

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house, so one piece goes inside the other
emptying the word of its interior leaves only its first and last letters

parts.note: the RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force

explanation.surface: A plane is caught emptying its cargo to make room for crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offloading contents' keeps only the ends of caught; 'to accommodate' houses the airmen between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft is a craft, a general word for any vessel or vehicle.

clue.text: Good Tory, concealing black binder

indicators.note: hiding a letter means it disappears from view, so it is removed

parts.note: blue is the Conservatives' colour, so a Tory is a blue
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A decent Conservative hiding a black folder.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the Conservative party colour; 'concealing' hides black's letter from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Glue binds things together, so it acts as an adhesive binder.

clue.text: Region classed as impoverished? Alderman to peeve, upset

indicators.note: upset letters are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A council official is annoyed that a district is officially labelled poor.
explanation.definitionFit: A development area was a British designation for a depressed region given state help for growth.

clue.text: Elderly friends accepting sport half-heartedly — inclined to play?

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: kith is an archaic word for friends, as in kith and kin

indicators.note: half the heart is lost: one of the two central letters goes

parts.note: tennis is a sport

explanation.surface: Old friends taking up a game without much enthusiasm, though they fancy a bit of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' loses one of the sport's two central letters; 'accepting' puts the rest inside the archaic word for friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Kittenish means playful and frisky, like a young cat.

clue.text: Poet rejected party with Society in it

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word reads in reverse

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: in signals one piece placed inside another

explanation.surface: A poet turned away from a society party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns DO into OD; then 'in' puts S into IT for IST.
explanation.definitionFit: An odist is a writer of odes, hence a poet.

clue.text: A lot of childhood disease linked to seaside location? I'd keep an eye on the games played

definitions.text: I'd keep an eye on the games played

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: croup is a respiratory illness of young children
a pier is a seaside landmark

explanation.surface: A sick child at the seaside, watched over by someone minding the games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' drops the disease's last letter. 'linked to' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A croupier runs a gambling table, overseeing roulette or card games in a casino.

clue.text: I toil desperately in support of reduced power: doing the right thing?

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece supporting another sits underneath it
reduced means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: punch means power or force

indicators.note: desperately suggests wild disorder, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Toiling desperately while low on power, wondering if it is the right thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts PUNCH to PUNC; 'desperately' rearranges I TOIL as TILIO, which 'in support of' places below.
explanation.definitionFit: Punctilio is a fine point of correct conduct, careful observance of etiquette.

clue.text: Rumour about new Government confusion

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a tale is a rumour or piece of gossip

explanation.surface: Gossip about a new administration causes confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts NG inside TALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangle is a muddled, twisted state, a mess or state of confusion.

clue.text: Likely to engage former car marque involved in type of motor racing

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside something

parts.note: the TT, Tourist Trophy, is motorcycle racing on the Isle of Man
Rover is a British car brand

explanation.surface: An old car brand is likely to take part in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' places the car marque inside the Isle of Man race initials; 'former' stands apart.
explanation.definitionFit: An extrovert is outgoing and sociable, keen to interact with others.

clue.text: Actors keeping record but disregarding a large source of influence

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: the cast is the set of actors in a show

indicators.note: disregarding means ignoring, so the letter is left out

parts.note: a tally is a running record or count
L is the abbreviation for large; a means just one of them

explanation.surface: Actors keep a record of the main influences on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disregarding' drops one L ('a large') from the record; 'keeping' places what remains inside the actors.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalyst is something that triggers change, an agent causing an effect.

clue.text: Gazing without seeing a lot of horses

indicators.note: without seeing means the named letter does not appear

parts.note: staring means gazing fixedly

explanation.surface: Gazing blindly at a herd of horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without seeing' removes A from STARING. 'Gazing' looks the definition, but 'a lot of horses' is.
explanation.definitionFit: A string is the set of racehorses kept by one trainer or stable.

clue.text: Film screened involving popular old woman

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so pieces go inside

parts.note: a film that ran was screened
in means popular or fashionable
ma is mother, informally the old woman

explanation.surface: A screened film involves a well-liked old lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' wraps 'screened' around the popular old woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain Man is the 1988 film starring Dustin Hoffman and Tom Cruise.

clue.text: Experienced a bird circling river, keeping on and on

indicators.note: circling means going around, enclosing another piece

parts.note: to have had something is to have experienced it
a tit is a small bird

explanation.surface: A bird keeps circling a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' has the word for experienced go round the river, before A and the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard at it is an idiom for working persistently without stopping.

clue.text: Wreck business with introduction of hopeless rep

indicators.note: introduction here means putting something into the middle

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss or business

indicators.note: hopeless suggests a mess, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A useless salesman ruins the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hopeless' turns REP into RPE, and 'with introduction of' inserts it into TODO.
explanation.definitionFit: To torpedo something is to sink it, figuratively to wreck it.

clue.text: Publican cornering one in lift

indicators.note: cornering means trapping, so one piece is hemmed in

parts.note: a publican is the host of a pub
I is the roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A landlord traps someone in an elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cornering' puts I inside HOST.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist is to raise up, especially with a pulley.

clue.text: Pick up time, getting encouragement

parts.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it

explanation.surface: Speeding up the pace brings encouragement.
explanation.definitionFit: To take heart is to be encouraged; heart here means courage or spirit.

clue.text: Chamber group accepting bit of Ravel's over fifteen minutes short

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a quartet is a chamber music ensemble

indicators.note: a bit of the name is only its first letter

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A string quartet takes a Ravel piece lasting over fifteen minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' places R inside QUARTET before its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter to an hour is fifteen minutes before it.

clue.text: Charlatan putting out constant source of error, making you tremble

indicators.note: putting out means ejecting, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a quack is a fake doctor
C is the scientific symbol for constant, as the speed of light

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A fraud's mistakes make you shake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting out' takes C out of QUACK, leaving QUAK.
explanation.definitionFit: To quake is to shake or shudder with fear.

clue.text: Rising worry about piano recording

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means reading upwards, in reverse
about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to eat someone is to worry them, as in what's eating you
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

explanation.surface: Growing anxiety over a piano recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts P inside EAT as EPAT, and 'Rising' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tape is magnetic recording media, and also a recording itself.

clue.text: Here's all primary working for astronomical device

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Everything basic gets built into an astronomical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: An armillary sphere is a model of the celestial globe made of rings.

clue.text: Painter and potter uncovered nonsense fool put about

indicators.note: put about means turned round, so the sequence reads backwards
uncovered means stripped of its outer letters

parts.note: rot means nonsense
a nit is a fool

explanation.surface: A painter and potter trade nonsense about a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' leaves OTTE from potter; OTTEROTNIT is then reversed by 'put about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tintoretto was a Venetian Renaissance artist.

clue.text: Pay for newspaper with nothing in it more than once

indicators.note: in signals one piece placed inside another

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times

indicators.note: more than once means the letter appears twice

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Paying for a newspaper that keeps carrying nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than once' doubles O, and 'in' places OO inside FT.
explanation.definitionFit: To foot the bill is to pay for it.
